domains.title: Cohort & Splitting
domains.description: Patient-level data partitioning, longitudinal and multi-scan grouping, locked held-out test isolation, consecutive eligibility, CONSORT/STARD participant flow, and sample-size justification.

domains.title: MRI Preprocessing & Harmonization
domains.description: Train-only fitting of intensity normalization and ComBat harmonization, sequence provenance and missing-modality handling, brain-extraction and post-op cavity QC, segmentation reliability, anisotropic resampling, and artifact screening.

domains.title: Radiomics & Foundation-Model Hygiene
domains.description: In-fold feature selection and oversampling hygiene, IBSI radiomics reproducibility, segmentation-perturbation ICC stability, foundation-model benchmark contamination audits, isolated hyperparameter tuning, and clinical/volumetric baseline ablations.

domains.title: Multi-Site & Shortcut Generalization
domains.description: External multi-institutional or temporal validation, scanner/vendor/site confounder shortcut audits, surgical and steroid artifact checks, label-prevalence and WHO-edition shift, global/pediatric subgroup equity, and OOD failure analysis.

domains.title: Clinical Calibration & Reference Standards
domains.description: WHO CNS5 (2021) integrated molecular reference alignment, RANO 2.0/RANO-BM/RANO-Resect outcome adjudication, probability calibration, patient-level uncertainty CIs, decision-curve clinical utility, and immortal-time landmarking.

domains.title: Open Science & Reproducibility
domains.description: Public code, preprocessing pipelines and inference release, explicit BraTS/TCGA partition case-ID manifests, deterministic compute disclosure, IRB/defacing/DICOM PHI compliance, CLAIM 2024 and TRIPOD+AI mapping, and non-SaMD clinical-use framing.

items.title: Patient-Level Partitioning (Zero 2D Slice/Patch Leakage)
items.question: Were train, validation, and test partitions constructed strictly at the unique patient level so that no 2D slices, 3D patches, or multiple exams from the same individual appear across splits?
items.failureMode: Splitting 2D axial MRI slices or 3D tumor patches randomly across train and test sets leaks patient-specific cranial geometry, sulcal patterns, coil bias fields, and tumor morphology—routinely inflating apparent AUROC from ~0.70 to >0.95 while collapsing on unseen patients.
items.remediation: Group all slices, patches, hemispheres, and exams by unique de-identified patient_id using StratifiedGroupKFold or site-grouped splits before any preprocessing, augmentation, or modeling, and run an automated zero-intersection assertion across split patient IDs.

items.title: Longitudinal & Multi-Scan Patient Grouping
items.question: When longitudinal surveillance MRIs, paired pre-/post-operative exams, multi-sequence acquisitions, or neurosurgical video frames are included, are all timepoints and frames from a given patient confined strictly to one partition?
items.failureMode: Placing a patient's baseline scan in training and a follow-up surveillance scan (or adjacent intraoperative video frames) in validation/test allows the network to memorize patient identity, resection-cavity shape, or surgical field illumination rather than generalizing biological progression.
items.remediation: Enforce patient-level (and procedure-level for surgical video) grouping across all longitudinal follow-ups and temporal frames, and verify that cross-cohort merges (e.g., TCGA-GBM with institutional archives or BraTS releases) deduplicate overlapping subjects.

items.title: Locked Held-Out Test Set & Nested Cross-Validation
items.question: Was a locked, untouched held-out test cohort (or strict outer loop of nested cross-validation) completely isolated from architecture iteration, feature selection, and operating-threshold selection?
items.failureMode: Repeatedly evaluating candidate models, radiomic signatures, or ensemble weights on the test set turns the test set into an implicit validation set, producing optimistic bias ('test-set overfitting') that fails prospective clinical deployment.
items.remediation: Freeze a single locked held-out test split (stratified by outcome, WHO CNS5 grade/subtype, and site) prior to model exploration, conduct all tuning inside nested cross-validation or a dedicated validation split, and evaluate the locked test set exactly once on the final pre-specified model.

items.title: Consecutive Cohort Eligibility & Spectrum Bias Reporting
items.question: Are explicit clinical inclusion/exclusion criteria, enrollment dates, care setting, and demographic breakdowns (age, sex, race/ethnicity, tumor subtype) reported to guard against case-control spectrum bias?
items.failureMode: Cherry-picking textbook extreme cases (e.g., large ring-enhancing GBM vs. classical non-enhancing LGG) while omitting indeterminate, small, or non-enhancing molecular GBMs creates spectrum bias and overstates real-world diagnostic performance.
items.remediation: Enroll a consecutive clinical cohort aligned to the intended neuro-oncology decision point, report recruitment dates and clinical setting, and provide a Table 1 demographic and molecular breakdown across train, internal validation, and external test sets.

items.title: Participant Flow & Exclusion Flowchart (CONSORT/STARD)
items.question: Does the study provide a complete CONSORT/STARD-style participant flow diagram accounting for every screened, excluded (missing MRI sequence, artifact, failed segmentation, missing molecular assay), and analyzed patient?
items.failureMode: Silent exclusion of difficult post-operative scans, motion-degraded exams, or incomplete sequences hides real-world failure rates and introduces non-random selection bias favoring clean academic scans.
items.remediation: Include a numbered CONSORT/STARD flow diagram enumerating screened cases, exact counts and reasons for every exclusion at each pipeline stage, and final patient/scan counts per partition.

items.title: Sample Size, Events-Per-Variable & Class-Balance Justification
items.question: Was the sample size justified against predictor dimensionality (events-per-variable / Riley criteria) with explicit reporting of class, grade, and site stratification across splits?
items.failureMode: Fitting high-dimensional radiomics (>1,000 features) or deep 3D CNNs on tiny neuro-oncology cohorts (<50 minority-class events) yields unstable weights, wide confidence intervals, and non-replicable biomarker signatures.
items.remediation: Report exact event counts per class and partition, justify sample size via formal power/precision or Riley et al. clinical prediction model criteria, and stratify splits by class, WHO CNS5 grade, and contributing center.

items.title: Train-Only Intensity Normalization, Scaling & ComBat Fitting
items.question: Were all cohort-level preprocessing statistics—intensity normalization parameters (z-score/Nyul/WhiteStripe), feature scalers, PCA transforms, and ComBat site-harmonization parameters—fit strictly inside training folds and applied out-of-sample to validation/test data?
items.failureMode: Fitting z-score scalers, histogram-matching landmarks, or NeuroCombat empirical-Bayes site parameters across the pooled dataset leaks test-set distribution moments (and outcome covariates if preserved in ComBat) into training, inflating external performance.
items.remediation: Encapsulate all scalers, PCA, and out-of-sample ComBat estimators inside an explicit training-fold pipeline (e.g., scikit-learn Pipeline / neuroHarmonize apply-only mode) so test scans are transformed using strictly frozen training statistics without access to test labels.

items.title: MRI Acquisition Protocol & Sequence Provenance (T1+C, FLAIR, 2D vs 3D)
items.question: Are MRI scanner vendors, field strengths (1.5T/3T/low-field), sequence parameters (T1, T1+C, T2, FLAIR, DWI/ADC, DSC; 2D vs 3D), and missing-modality handling explicitly documented?
items.failureMode: Unreported heterogeneity in slice thickness, 2D spin-echo vs. 3D MPRAGE T1+C, gadolinium timing, or ad-hoc imputation of missing sequences introduces silent domain shifts and brittle inference when clinical protocols vary.
items.remediation: Tabulate scanner manufacturers, field strengths, voxel spacing, TE/TR ranges, and contrast protocols per site, and specify how missing sequences are handled (e.g., modality-dropout training, synthesis validation, or explicit protocol eligibility).

items.title: Brain Extraction, Co-Registration & Resection-Cavity QC
items.question: Were N4 bias-field correction, skull-stripping (brain extraction), inter-sequence/atlas co-registration targets, and interpolation orders specified with explicit failure QC—especially on post-operative resection cavities?
items.failureMode: Standard brain-extraction tools (e.g., BET) frequently clip peripheral meningiomas, dural-based lesions, or post-craniotomy resection cavities, while aggressive nonlinear registration distorts mass effect and midline shift.
items.remediation: Use tumor-validated skull-stripping (e.g., HD-BET or SynthStrip), state rigid vs. affine/deformable registration targets and label nearest-neighbor interpolation, and log visual QC failure rates and manual correction counts on pre-op and post-op cavities.

items.title: Ground-Truth Tumor Segmentation Protocol & Inter-Rater Reliability (Dice)
items.question: Were tumor sub-region definitions (enhancing core, necrotic core, non-enhancing FLAIR infiltration), annotator qualifications, consensus adjudication, and inter-rater spatial/boundary agreement (Dice and HD95/ASSD) reported?
items.failureMode: Ambiguous or single-novice ROI boundaries introduce systematic label noise—especially in ill-defined non-enhancing IDH-mutant gliomas and post-op cavities—making downstream volumetric, RANO-Resect, and radiomics outputs unrepeatable.
items.remediation: Define sub-compartments using standardized BraTS/RANO conventions, have board-certified neuroradiologists adjudicate masks blinded to clinical outcomes, and quantify inter-rater variability with both volumetric Dice and boundary metrics (HD95/ASSD).

items.title: Isotropic Resampling & Anisotropic Slice-Thickness Handling
items.question: Is native voxel anisotropy (e.g., 5 mm clinical 2D slices vs. 1 mm 3D isotropic) reported alongside a principled resampling strategy (3D isotropic vs. 2.5D/in-plane) that avoids through-plane interpolation artifacts?
items.failureMode: Upsampling thick 5 mm 2D clinical MRI slices to 1 mm³ isotropic with cubic interpolation fabricates synthetic through-plane texture patterns that corrupt 3D GLCM/GLRLM radiomics and break 3D CNN receptive-field assumptions.
items.remediation: Report native in-plane resolution and slice thickness distributions; prefer 2D/2.5D extraction or anisotropic kernels when slice thickness exceeds 3× in-plane spacing, and document exact interpolation orders for images (B-spline/linear) vs. binary masks (nearest-neighbor).

items.title: Motion, Susceptibility & Post-Op Blood-Product Artifact QA
items.question: Was a systematic imaging quality-assurance protocol applied to detect motion ghosting, metal/susceptibility distortion, and early post-operative T1-hyperintense blood products (with pre-contrast T1 subtraction where relevant)?
items.failureMode: Post-operative methemoglobin blood products appear intrinsically bright on T1+C and mimic residual contrast-enhancing tumor, falsely downgrading RANO-Resect classes and confounding post-op segmentation/prognosis models.
items.remediation: Implement a reproducible pre-analysis QA rubric checking motion, titanium-plate susceptibility, and pre- vs. post-contrast T1 comparison (within 24–72 h post-op), documenting both excluded artifacts and model robustness on borderline-quality scans.

items.title: In-Fold Feature Selection, Dimensionality Reduction & Oversampling (SMOTE)
items.question: Were all supervised feature selection steps (LASSO, mRMR, univariate p-filtering, RFE), dimensionality reduction, data augmentation, and class oversampling (SMOTE/ADASYN) performed strictly inside each training fold?
items.failureMode: Running LASSO/univariate feature selection or SMOTE on the entire cohort before cross-validation leaks test labels and creates near-duplicate synthetic minority samples across train and test folds—one of the most prevalent invalidators of published radiomics studies.
items.remediation: Nest all univariate screens, LASSO/mRMR selectors, PCA, spatial augmentations, and oversampling strictly inside each inner training fold via an end-to-end Pipeline; never apply SMOTE or test-time augmentation leakage to validation or test partitions.

items.title: IBSI-Compliant Radiomics Extraction Parameters (Bin Width, Filters)
items.question: For handcrafted radiomics or hybrid models, are IBSI-compliant extraction parameters (fixed bin width vs. bin count, LoG sigmas, wavelet basis, aggregation mode, and software version/YAML) fully disclosed?
items.failureMode: Small undisclosed differences in gray-level discretization (bin count vs. fixed bin width), intensity re-segmentation, or filter padding drastically alter texture feature values, rendering radiomic signatures non-reproducible across institutions.
items.remediation: Follow Image Biomarker Standardisation Initiative (IBSI) definitions, report exact discretization and filter settings, and publish the complete PyRadiomics/CaPTk parameter YAML file alongside the manuscript.

items.title: Radiomic Feature Repeatability & Segmentation-Perturbation Stability (ICC)
items.question: Were candidate imaging features audited for repeatability against multi-rater segmentation variability or mask perturbations (ICC/CCC thresholds) and label-noise bounds?
items.failureMode: High-order texture features frequently collapse under minor 1–2 voxel tumor boundary shifts or scanner re-scans, causing fragile models whose predictions flip when a different neuroradiologist or automated network segments the tumor.
items.remediation: Quantify feature stability via inter-rater double segmentations or controlled morphological mask perturbations (within training data only), retaining robust features (e.g., ICC ≥ 0.75–0.85) and reporting sensitivity to automated vs. manual masks.

items.title: Foundation-Model / Pretrained Backbone Benchmark Contamination Audit
items.question: If a medical foundation model, self-supervised 3D encoder, or pretrained neuroimaging backbone is used, was its pretraining corpus audited for patient/case overlap against the evaluation benchmarks (e.g., BraTS, TCGA-GBM/LGG, UPenn-GBM, UCSF-PDGM, UK Biobank)?
items.failureMode: Public brain-tumor benchmarks share heavily overlapping TCGA, BraTS, UPenn-GBM, and UCSF-PDGM subjects; fine-tuning or zero-shot evaluating a foundation model pretrained on those corpora causes severe benchmark contamination and inflated generalization claims.
items.remediation: Document the exact pretraining datasets and release versions of every foundation/pretrained backbone, cross-check BraTS/TCIA subject mapping tables to remove any overlapping patients from test sets, and confirm true out-of-corpus external evaluation.

items.title: Hyperparameter Tuning & Checkpoint Selection Isolated from Test Set
items.question: Were hyperparameter searches, early-stopping epochs, model architecture comparisons, and ensemble weights selected strictly using validation folds—never by inspecting test-set performance?
items.failureMode: Selecting the best checkpoint epoch, classifier family, or fusion weight by maximizing test-set AUC or Dice leaks evaluation feedback directly into model selection, biasing reported accuracy upward by 5–15 points.
items.remediation: Freeze all hyperparameters, stopping rules, and model-selection criteria strictly on internal validation folds (or inner nested CV), log the single pre-specified winner prior to test evaluation, and report both validation and untouched test metrics.

items.title: Incremental Value Ablation Against Clinical/Volumetric Baseline
items.question: Was the AI/radiomics model rigorously ablated against parsimonious clinical and simple volumetric baselines (e.g., age, KPS, tumor volume, anatomical location, RANO-Resect EOR) to demonstrate true incremental value?
items.failureMode: Complex 3D deep learning or 1,000-feature radiomic survival models frequently merely rediscover tumor volume or patient age without improving C-index, calibration, or clinical decision-making over routine clinical variables.
items.remediation: Benchmark the imaging model alone, clinical/volumetric baseline alone, and combined multimodal model on identical splits using statistical comparisons (e.g., ΔAUROC, ΔC-index, likelihood ratio, or net benefit).

items.title: True External Multi-Institutional or Temporal Validation Cohort
items.question: Was final model performance validated on an independent external multi-institutional cohort (different hospitals/scanners) or, when infeasible, a clearly separated prospective/temporal external cohort?
items.failureMode: Single-center internal cross-validation dramatically overestimates generalizability in neuro-oncology because models exploit institution-specific MRI protocols, referral patterns, and surgical practices that break across hospitals.
items.remediation: Evaluate the frozen final model without re-tuning on at least one geographically independent external hospital cohort (and/or prospective temporal cohort), reporting external performance as the primary generalizability endpoint.

items.title: Scanner, Vendor & Site-Confounder Shortcut Audit
items.question: Did the authors audit whether model predictions exploit hospital site, MRI vendor, field strength, or acquisition protocol as a shortcut proxy for tumor grade, molecular status, or outcome?
items.failureMode: When molecular subtypes or tumor grades differ in prevalence across hospitals or scanners (e.g., pediatric vs. adult centers, 3T research vs. 1.5T community MRIs), neural networks achieve high pooled AUC by classifying hospital/scanner identity rather than tumor biology.
items.remediation: Report per-site and per-scanner stratified performance, probe learned embeddings for site/vendor predictability, audit background/non-tumor shortcut sensitivity, and verify that site-stratified metrics remain robust.

items.title: Surgical/Treatment Artifact Shortcut Check (Craniotomy, Cavity, Steroids)
items.question: Were potential treatment-related shortcuts and pre-op vs. post-treatment domain shifts audited—including craniotomy defects, resection cavities, hemostatic agents, radiotherapy changes, and corticosteroid dosing?
items.failureMode: Models trained across mixed pre-/post-op scans or unadjusted steroid regimens may latch onto surgical hardware, resection cavities, or steroid-suppressed FLAIR edema as spurious cues for diagnosis, progression, or pseudoprogression.
items.remediation: Explicitly separate pre-operative and post-treatment cohorts, audit performance across resection status and steroid exposure, and verify saliency maps do not activate on skull defects, surgical staples, or non-brain margins.

items.title: Cross-Site Label Prevalence & WHO-Edition Shift Assessment
items.question: Were cross-site differences in outcome prevalence, referral-center case mix, and diagnostic WHO edition shifts (WHO 2007/2016 vs. WHO CNS5 2021) analyzed when interpreting external metrics?
items.failureMode: External cohorts with different IDH-mutation prevalence or legacy WHO 2016 grading exhibit marked shifts in PPV/NPV and calibration intercept even when discrimination appears unchanged, misleading clinical threshold deployment.
items.remediation: Compare class prevalence, molecular testing coverage, and WHO CNS5 reclassification rates between development and external cohorts, reporting prevalence-sensitive metrics (PPV, NPV, AUPRC, calibration-in-the-large) alongside AUROC.

items.title: Subgroup Performance & Equity Stratification (Age, Sex, Subtype, EOR)
items.question: Is model performance stratified across key clinical and equity subgroups—including age, sex, molecular subtype, extent of resection, and underrepresented low-field/global or pediatric cohorts (e.g., BraTS-Africa, BraTS-PEDs) where applicable?
items.failureMode: Strong aggregate metrics on high-resource adult 3T cohorts routinely conceal severe performance degradation in younger/older patients, rare molecular subtypes, pediatric midline gliomas, or low-field (<1.5T) scanners in resource-constrained settings.
items.remediation: Report subgroup discrimination, segmentation accuracy, and calibration across age, sex, WHO CNS5 subtype, EOR, and scanner field strength (highlighting representation gaps such as low-field or pediatric populations when external data are absent).

items.title: Saliency, Failure-Case & Out-of-Distribution (OOD) Qualitative Audit
items.question: Did the study perform qualitative failure-case inspection, neuroradiologist review of misclassified/worst-segmented cases, and out-of-distribution (OOD) stress testing (e.g., CNS lymphoma, metastasis, or abscess mimics)?
items.failureMode: Reporting only mean Dice or AUROC hides catastrophic failure modes—such as missing small enhancing satellite nodules, segmenting normal choroid plexus, or overconfidently classifying brain abscesses or PCNSL as glioblastoma.
items.remediation: Present systematic error taxonomies of top false-positive/false-negative and lowest-Dice cases reviewed by neuroradiologists, pair saliency checks with quantitative perturbation tests, and characterize OOD behavior on non-glioma mimics.

items.title: WHO CNS5 (2021) Integrated Molecular Reference Standard Alignment
items.question: Are histopathologic and molecular ground-truth labels aligned to the WHO CNS5 (2021) integrated classification (IDH1/2 sequencing, 1p/19q, CDKN2A/B homdel, TERT/EGFR/+7/-10, H3 K27/G34) rather than outdated histology-only grades?
items.failureMode: Legacy WHO 2007/2016 labels misclassify IDH-mutant grade 4 astrocytomas as 'glioblastoma' and mislabel molecularly upgraded IDH-wildtype GBMs as 'low-grade gliomas', corrupting both biological validity and therapeutic relevance.
items.remediation: Re-adjudicate legacy cohorts (including TCGA-GBM/LGG) to WHO CNS5 (2021) criteria using molecular markers, explicitly flag cases lacking required molecular assays as NOS, and report exact assay methods (IHC vs. IDH1/2 sequencing, FISH/NGS).

items.title: Standardized Clinical Response / Outcome Adjudication (RANO 2.0 / RANO-BM)
items.question: Are clinical endpoints adjudicated using standardized neuro-oncology criteria—such as RANO 2.0, RANO-BM, or RANO-Resect, and for segmentation tasks, volumetric Dice paired with clinically meaningful boundary metrics (HD95/ASSD)?
items.failureMode: Unstandardized progression definitions ignoring corticosteroid escalation, early post-RT pseudoprogression (≤12 weeks), or relying solely on Dice without HD95/ASSD boundary errors disconnect AI outputs from clinical trial and surgical endpoints.
items.remediation: Adjudicate response and resection endpoints strictly per RANO 2.0, RANO-BM, or RANO-Resect with blinded central review where feasible; pair Dice with 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), ASSD, and clinically relevant volume-error bounds.

items.title: Probability Calibration Reporting (Calibration Slope/Intercept, Brier, ECE)
items.question: Is discrimination (AUROC/C-index) paired with formal probability calibration assessment—specifically calibration slope, calibration-in-the-large intercept, Brier score, ECE, and smoothed reliability curves on external data?
items.failureMode: Modern neural networks and boosted trees are notoriously overconfident despite strong AUROC; miscalibrated risk probabilities mislead neuro-oncology tumor-board counseling, biopsy decisions, and trial stratification.
items.remediation: Report flexible calibration curves, calibration slope and intercept, Brier score (or integrated Brier score for survival), and Expected Calibration Error (ECE); if post-hoc recalibration (Platt/temperature scaling) is used, fit it strictly on validation data.

items.title: Uncertainty Quantification & Patient-Level Confidence Intervals (Bootstrap/IPCW)
items.question: Are all primary performance estimates accompanied by patient-level statistical uncertainty intervals (e.g., cluster/patient bootstrap CIs, IPCW for censored survival, multiple-testing corrections) and predictive uncertainty or abstention behavior?
items.failureMode: Reporting bare point estimates or slice-level confidence intervals violates patient-level independence and dramatically understates estimation error, while omitting predictive uncertainty prevents safe deferral on ambiguous scans.
items.remediation: Compute 95% confidence intervals via patient-clustered bootstrapping (or IPCW/DeLong at the patient level), adjust p-values for multiple hypothesis testing, and evaluate uncertainty-guided abstention or selective-prediction trade-offs.

items.title: Clinical Utility, Operating-Point Justification & Decision Curve Analysis
items.question: Are decision thresholds justified clinically in advance and evaluated via Decision Curve Analysis (net benefit across clinically relevant risk thresholds) or clinical-utility workflow modeling?
items.failureMode: Optimizing post-hoc Youden thresholds on test ROC curves ignores the asymmetric clinical harms of false negatives vs. false positives in neurosurgery (e.g., withholding resection or misdirecting targeted therapy).
items.remediation: Pre-specify operating points aligned to clinical harm-benefit trade-offs (e.g., high-sensitivity screening vs. high-specificity rule-in), report sensitivity/specificity/PPV/NPV at those locked thresholds, and include Decision Curve Analysis against treat-all and treat-none strategies.

items.title: Immortal-Time Bias & Future-Treatment Leakage Guard (Landmarking)
items.question: Are all input features strictly restricted to information available at the prediction index timepoint (proper landmarking), preventing immortal-time bias or future-treatment leakage (e.g., post-op EOR or adjuvant RT fed into pre-op predictors)?
items.failureMode: Including post-baseline variables (such as completion of 6 cycles of temozolomide, extent of resection, or 3-month post-RT MRI features) to predict survival from diagnosis introduces immortal-time bias and temporal target leakage, invalidating clinical use at baseline.
items.remediation: Define an explicit prediction index time (e.g., pre-operative MRI or 4-week post-RT landmark), exclude any variable ascertained after that landmark, and align survival follow-up origin strictly to the landmark date.

items.title: Public Code, Preprocessing Pipeline & Inference Model Availability
items.question: Are complete preprocessing scripts, training/evaluation code, and trained inference weights or reproducible containers (Docker/Singularity) publicly released in a persistent repository?
items.failureMode: 'Code available upon reasonable request' rarely results in usable replication, leaving hidden preprocessing bugs, split leakage, and undocumented post-processing heuristics unverifiable by independent teams.
items.remediation: Publish complete end-to-end preprocessing, training, and inference code under an OSI license on GitHub/Zenodo with a DOI, and release frozen model weights or a containerized inference package whenever governance permits.

items.title: Explicit Cohort Manifest & Partition Case-IDs (BraTS/TCGA Replication)
items.question: Are exact case-ID manifests and train/validation/test partition assignments published for public neuro-oncology datasets (BraTS, TCGA, UPenn-GBM, UCSF-PDGM) to enable independent replication?
items.failureMode: Without exact subject-level split CSVs for public datasets like BraTS or TCGA-GBM, independent researchers cannot verify zero patient overlap, reproduce benchmark comparisons, or detect cherry-picked test subsets.
items.remediation: Release a machine-readable CSV manifest listing public TCIA/BraTS subject IDs, scan timepoints, WHO CNS5 label mappings, exclusion flags, and exact fold/split assignments as supplemental material.

items.title: Deterministic Seeds, Library Versions & Compute Environment Disclosure
items.question: Are random seeds, exact deep-learning/radiomics software library versions, hardware specifications, training compute time, and inference latency disclosed?
items.failureMode: Undisclosed PyTorch/MONAI/nnU-Net/PyRadiomics versions and unseeded stochastic pipelines cause silent numerical drift and prevent hospitals from assessing real-world clinical compute feasibility.
items.remediation: Pin exact dependencies (requirements.txt/conda lockfile), set and log random seeds across multi-seed runs to quantify training variance, and report GPU architecture, training hours, and per-patient inference latency.

items.title: IRB/Ethics Approval, Defacing & DICOM De-Identification Protocol
items.question: Are IRB/ethics approval, informed-consent or waiver status, data-use agreements, DICOM-to-NIfTI PHI header scrubbing, and 3D cranial MRI defacing/de-identification protocols explicitly documented?
items.failureMode: High-resolution 3D T1/FLAIR brain MRIs permit accurate facial reconstruction via surface rendering, and uncleaned DICOM private tags or burned-in overlays can leak Protected Health Information (PHI) during sharing or model training.
items.remediation: Document IRB protocol numbers and data-use compliance, strip all DICOM PHI headers during NIfTI conversion with automated verification, and apply validated defacing (e.g., PyDeface/mri_deface) or skull-stripping prior to any multi-site sharing.

items.title: Completed CLAIM 2024 & TRIPOD+AI Cross-Reference Supplement
items.question: Does the manuscript include a completed, section-referenced CLAIM 2024 and/or TRIPOD+AI reporting checklist supplement?
items.failureMode: Omitting structured reporting supplements slows peer review and allows critical methodological omissions (split hygiene, calibration, external cohort provenance) to go unnoticed in dense prose.
items.remediation: Attach a completed CLAIM 2024 and TRIPOD+AI cross-reference table mapping every checklist item to exact manuscript page/section numbers or explaining why an item is not applicable.

items.title: Intended-Use Scope, Human-in-the-Loop Limits & Non-SaMD Framing
items.question: Are intended clinical role, target population boundaries, human-in-the-loop neuroradiology/tumor-board oversight requirements, and non-autonomous / Non-SaMD regulatory limitations clearly stated?
items.failureMode: Overclaiming autonomous diagnostic accuracy for retrospective research prototypes risks unsafe off-label clinical reliance and obscures the prospective regulatory validation required for Software as a Medical Device (SaMD).
items.remediation: Explicitly define intended use (e.g., research decision-support adjunct for multidisciplinary neuro-oncology review), enumerate contraindicated clinical scenarios, and clearly state non-autonomous / Non-SaMD research status.

gold_standard.label: Gold Standard Multi-Center Study
gold_standard.description: High-rigor multi-institutional prospective external validation study for WHO CNS5 IDH1/2 and 1p/19q radiogenomics with patient-level splits, train-only preprocessing, foundation-model deduplication, calibration, and full open-science artifacts.

studyMeta.title: Multi-Center 3D Radiogenomic Classification of Adult-Type Diffuse Gliomas Under WHO CNS5 Criteria: A Prospective External Validation Study
studyMeta.authors: Patel R, Lindholm K, Okonkwo C, et al.
studyMeta.modality: Multi-parametric 1.5T/3T MRI (T1, T1+C, T2, FLAIR, ADC)
studyMeta.cohortSummary: n=1,148 consecutive adult diffuse glioma patients across 7 centers (n=762 development; n=386 geographically & temporally external test)

CS-01.evidence: Methods p. 6: Strict patient-level StratifiedGroupKFold (k=5) by unique patient_id; automated zero-overlap unit test verified in repo.

CS-02.evidence: Methods p. 6: Single pre-operative diagnostic MRI per patient; cross-registry TCIA/institutional deduplication confirmed zero duplicate subjects.

CS-03.evidence: Methods p. 7: External 3-center cohort (n=386) locked before model development and evaluated exactly once on the pre-specified final model.

CS-04.evidence: Methods p. 5 & Table 1: Consecutive adult diffuse gliomas (2018-2024) with complete age, sex, race/ethnicity, and molecular subtype distributions.

CS-05.evidence: Fig. 1: Full STARD flow diagram enumerating 1,312 screened patients and exact exclusion reasons (missing T1+C n=74, non-glioma n=58, incomplete molecular n=32).

CS-06.evidence: Methods p. 5 & Supp. Note 1: Riley et al. minimum sample-size calculation verified (>140 minority-class 1p/19q-codeleted events); site- and grade-stratified splits.

MP-01.evidence: Methods p. 8: WhiteStripe normalization and out-of-sample neuroHarmonize ComBat parameters fit exclusively on each training fold and applied frozen to test scans.

MP-02.evidence: Supp. Table S1: Scanner vendors (Siemens, GE, Philips), 1.5T/3T field strengths, TR/TE, 2D/3D sequence breakdown, and modality-dropout protocol reported.

MP-03.evidence: Methods p. 8: N4ITK bias correction, HD-BET skull-stripping, and ANTs rigid co-registration to T1+C with manual neuroradiologist QC (1.4% mask correction rate logged).

MP-04.evidence: Methods p. 9: Dual board-certified neuroradiologist adjudication on BraTS sub-regions; inter-rater Dice 0.91 (WT) / 0.88 (ET) and median HD95 2.4 mm.

MP-05.evidence: Methods p. 8: Native voxel spacing distributions reported; 1x1x1 mm3 B-spline resampling for 3D sequences and anisotropic-aware 2.5D fusion evaluated for thick-slice 2D scans.

MP-06.evidence: Methods p. 9 & Supp. Fig. S2: Pre-analysis MRI artifact QA rubric documented; motion-corrupted scans quantified separately in robustness sensitivity analysis.

RF-01.evidence: Methods p. 10: All feature filtering, mRMR/LASSO selection, class weighting, and 3D spatial augmentations nested strictly inside each inner training fold.

RF-02.evidence: Methods p. 10 & GitHub YAML: IBSI-compliant PyRadiomics v3.1.0 fixed bin width 25, LoG sigmas [1, 2, 3 mm], and coif1 wavelets published verbatim.

RF-03.evidence: Supp. Table S2: Segmentation-perturbation stability (±2 mm dilation/erosion + inter-rater masks inside training folds) retained features with ICC ≥ 0.85.

RF-04.evidence: Methods p. 11: Self-supervised SwinUNETR backbone pretrained exclusively on non-overlapping healthy/stroke MRI corpora; zero BraTS/TCGA/UPenn-GBM/UCSF-PDGM overlap audited.

RF-05.evidence: Methods p. 11: Hyperparameters, early stopping, and ensemble weights selected strictly via inner 5-fold CV without querying external test metrics.

RF-06.evidence: Results Table 2: Multimodal model (AUROC 0.91) outperformed clinical+volumetric baseline (age, location, necrosis volume; AUROC 0.78, DeLong p < 0.001).

MS-01.evidence: Results p. 13: External validation across 3 geographically independent hospitals including a prospective 2023-2024 enrollment cohort (n=386).

MS-02.evidence: Results p. 14 & Supp. Table S4: Per-site (AUROC 0.88-0.93) and per-vendor (1.5T vs 3T) stratification plus linear site-probe on latent embeddings (site AUC 0.54).

MS-03.evidence: Methods p. 6 & Supp. Fig. S4: Strictly pre-operative MRIs; sensitivity analysis stratified by pre-op dexamethasone exposure showed stable discrimination (ΔAUROC 0.01).

MS-04.evidence: Results p. 13 & Table 1: Cross-site IDH-mutant prevalence shift (26% dev vs. 34% external) explicitly reported with AUPRC, PPV, NPV, and calibration intercept.

MS-05.evidence: Results Table 3 stratifies by age, sex, and WHO CNS5 subtype; however, ultra-low-field (<1.5T) and sub-Saharan/global scanners (e.g., BraTS-Africa) were not represented.

MS-06.evidence: Fig. 4 includes neuroradiologist review of 12 misclassified cases and Grad-CAM checks, though formal OOD stress testing against CNS lymphoma/abscess mimics was limited to a small pilot (n=18).

CC-01.evidence: Methods p. 6: All diagnoses centrally adjudicated to WHO CNS5 (2021) using IDH1/2 sequencing, 1p/19q FISH/NGS, CDKN2A/B, TERT, EGFR, and +7/-10 status.

CC-02.evidence: N/A: Study targets pre-operative WHO CNS5 molecular diagnosis rather than longitudinal post-treatment RANO 2.0 / RANO-BM response adjudication.

CC-03.evidence: Results Fig. 3: External calibration curve reported (slope 0.96, intercept -0.04, Brier 0.098, ECE 0.031) with validation-fit temperature scaling.

CC-04.evidence: Results Table 2 & Fig. 3B: Patient-level 2,000-replicate bootstrap 95% CIs, Holm-Bonferroni correction, and uncertainty-abstention curve deferring 10% highest-entropy cases.

CC-05.evidence: Fig. 5 presents Decision Curve Analysis across 10%-50% risk thresholds with pre-specified operating point, though prospective clinical-workflow impact study remains ongoing.

CC-06.evidence: Methods p. 6: All MRI and clinical predictors strictly restricted to pre-operative index timepoint; zero surgical, EOR, or post-op adjuvant features entered.

OS-01.evidence: Data Availability p. 18: Full preprocessing/training code, Docker inference container, and frozen weights released on GitHub & Zenodo (MIT license).

OS-02.evidence: Supp. Data 1: Complete de-identified subject manifest and exact train/val/test case-ID CSVs published for all public TCIA/BraTS benchmark subsets.

OS-03.evidence: Conda lockfile, PyTorch/MONAI versions, GPU hardware, and inference latency (11.2 s/case) disclosed; multi-seed variance across 3 seeds reported only for primary model.

OS-04.evidence: Ethics p. 17: Multi-center IRB approvals, DUAs, automated DICOM-to-NIfTI PHI scrubbing, and HD-BET/PyDeface cranial defacing documented.

OS-05.evidence: Supp. Tables S6-S7: Completed CLAIM 2024 (44-item) and TRIPOD+AI (27-item) checklists mapped to exact manuscript page numbers.

OS-06.evidence: Discussion p. 16: Explicit research-only Non-SaMD framing stating model is a human-in-the-loop adjunct and cannot replace neuropathological molecular confirmation.

slice_leakage_pitfall.label: Slice-Leakage Radiomics Pitfall (Blocker Cap Demo)
slice_leakage_pitfall.description: Classic high-leakage single-center 2D slice-split glioblastoma radiomics + SMOTE study that scores ~59% raw weighted points on documentation/extraction items yet triggers the automated 45/100 Critical Blocker cap due to fatal leakage flaws (CS-01, MP-01, RF-01, MS-01, CC-01).

studyMeta.title: High-Accuracy 2D Slice-Based Radiomics and Gradient Boosting for Glioblastoma Molecular Subtyping: A Single-Center Retrospective Study
studyMeta.authors: Chen L, Morales D, et al. (Synthetic Pitfall Archetype)
studyMeta.taskType: Radiomics Classification (2D Slice-Split Glioma Grading / IDH)
studyMeta.cohortSummary: n=142 retrospective single-center glioma patients (2,840 pooled 2D axial tumor slices randomly split 80/20)

CS-01.evidence: CRITICAL BLOCKER — Methods p. 4: 2,840 2D axial tumor slices from 142 patients were pooled and randomly split 80/20 at the slice level, placing adjacent slices of identical patients in both train and test sets (inflated test AUC 0.97).

CS-02.evidence: Methods p. 3: Single baseline pre-operative MRI per patient included; no longitudinal follow-up scans used.

CS-03.evidence: Methods p. 5: A 20% slice-split holdout existed, but the authors iteratively compared 6 classifier architectures directly against the holdout test AUC.

CS-04.evidence: Methods p. 3 & Table 1: Consecutive single-center surgical cohort (2014-2021) with basic age and sex demographics reported.

CS-05.evidence: Fig. 1: Flow diagram reports exclusion counts for severe motion (n=9) and missing FLAIR sequence (n=14).

CS-06.evidence: Methods p. 4: Severe class imbalance (118 GBM vs. 24 IDH-mutant) with 1,218 candidate features and zero sample-size or events-per-variable justification.

MP-01.evidence: CRITICAL BLOCKER — Methods p. 4: Z-score intensity normalization and radiomic feature standardization (StandardScaler) were fit across all 2,840 slices prior to train/test splitting.

MP-02.evidence: Supp. Table S1: Single Siemens 3T Skyra scanner protocol, TR/TE, and T1+C/FLAIR sequence settings tabulated.

MP-03.evidence: Methods p. 4: BET skull-stripping and ANTs rigid registration to T1+C visually checked on all pre-operative scans.

MP-04.evidence: Methods p. 4: Two neuroradiologists delineated whole-tumor ROIs in ITK-SNAP (inter-rater Dice 0.87 reported).

MP-05.evidence: Methods p. 4: Native spacing stated; images resampled to 1x1x1 mm3 via B-spline interpolation prior to 2D slice export.

MP-06.evidence: Severe motion artifacts excluded at screening, but no standardized susceptibility or contrast-timing QA rubric documented.

RF-01.evidence: CRITICAL BLOCKER — Methods p. 5: LASSO feature selection (1,218 -> 14 features) and SMOTE synthetic minority oversampling were applied to the full dataset before 5-fold cross-validation and test splitting.

RF-02.evidence: Methods p. 5: PyRadiomics v3.0.1 fixed bin width 25, LoG sigmas [1, 2, 3], and wavelet filter settings documented.

RF-03.evidence: Methods p. 5: Inter-rater ICC ≥ 0.75 repeatability filter applied on 20 double-segmented cases (though computed outside CV).

RF-04.evidence: N/A: Handcrafted PyRadiomics + XGBoost tabular pipeline only; no pretrained deep foundation model or external imaging weights used.

RF-05.evidence: Hyperparameter grid search ran inside 5-fold CV, but final model family (XGBoost vs. SVM/RF) was chosen based on highest test-set AUC.

RF-06.evidence: Results Table 2: Compared against a clinical baseline logistic model (age + KPS).

MS-01.evidence: CRITICAL BLOCKER — Discussion p. 11: Single-center internal slice split only; zero external multi-institutional or temporal validation cohort.

MS-02.evidence: Single 3T scanner eliminates multi-vendor confounding internally, but no protocol-shift or background-shortcut probe was performed.

MS-03.evidence: Strictly pre-operative scans avoid surgical cavity artifacts, but pre-operative dexamethasone steroid exposure was neither recorded nor adjusted.

MS-04.evidence: No label-prevalence or WHO-edition shift analysis; 2014-2016 histology-only cases were pooled directly with post-2016 molecularly tested cases.

MS-05.evidence: Subgroup AUC shown for age ≥60 vs. <60 only; sex, tumor location, molecular subtype, and scanner generalizations omitted.

MS-06.evidence: Fig. 5: SHAP feature-importance summary plot and 2 misclassified failure cases qualitatively illustrated.

CC-01.evidence: CRITICAL BLOCKER — Methods p. 3: Ground-truth labels rely on legacy WHO 2007/2016 histology ('Grade IV GBM' including IDH-mutant astrocytomas) without CDKN2A/B, TERT, EGFR, or +7/-10 adjudication.

CC-02.evidence: Methods p. 3: Secondary overall-survival endpoint adjudicated from institutional cancer registry mortality dates.

CC-03.evidence: Fig. 4A plots a calibration curve, but calibration slope, intercept, Brier score, and ECE are omitted.

CC-04.evidence: 95% DeLong CIs reported, but computed at the non-independent 2D slice level rather than clustered by patient; no predictive uncertainty abstention.

CC-05.evidence: Fig. 4B includes Decision Curve Analysis across threshold probabilities 0.1-0.8.

CC-06.evidence: Methods p. 3: Predictors restricted to pre-operative MRI and baseline clinical demographics; no post-op treatment variables leaked.

OS-01.evidence: PyRadiomics YAML provided in supplement, but splitting and XGBoost training scripts marked 'available upon reasonable request'.

OS-02.evidence: Private institutional cohort; summary Table 1 reported without a de-identified split manifest.

OS-03.evidence: Methods p. 5: Python 3.10, PyRadiomics 3.0.1, scikit-learn 1.3.2, XGBoost 2.0, and random_state=42 specified.

OS-04.evidence: Ethics p. 12: Institutional IRB approval number, retrospective consent waiver, and HIPAA DICOM de-identification stated.

OS-05.evidence: Legacy CLAIM 2020 checklist attached without CLAIM 2024 or TRIPOD+AI section mapping.

OS-06.evidence: Discussion p. 11: States research-only prototype status requiring prospective multi-center validation before clinical use.
